description: Andrei Faragau and colleagues provide MATLAB and Maple code for vehicle-track interaction at railway transition zones. The linked TU Delft publication abstract describes an infinite Euler-Bernoulli rail beam on a locally variable Kelvin foundation, coupled to a moving loaded oscillator through a nonlinear Hertzian spring. Green functions, finite differences and non-reflective boundaries solve the beam-foundation subsystem. Wheel-rail contact force and vehicle power or energy input are proposed as degradation indicators for structural-design simulations of railway transitions. 4TU.ResearchData provides the code freely under CC BY 4.0, listing 45 file descriptors including scripts and a supporting document. The paper appeared in 2020; the deposit was published in May 2025. Coverage is an idealised track transition, without a stated real railway location. The abstract describes numerical comparisons with moving constant loads, but does not establish field validation or predictive accuracy. Runtime requirements and full parameter definitions remain unknown because no code or document body was downloaded. The related nonlinear-foundation model uses a different loading formulation.
